o.text: From Proto-Turkic *kök (“root”). Cognate with Chuvash кӑк (kăk, “root, base”).
From Persian کلم (kalam), ultimately from Ancient Greek κράμβη (krámbē, “cabbage”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian گناهکار (gunāh-kār). By surface analysis, günah + -kar.
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish ارن (ẹren, eren), from Proto-Turkic *ēren, the irregular plural of Proto-Turkic *ēr (“man”). Cognate with Kazakh ерен (eren).
Onomatopoeic. Equivalent to vız (“buzzing sound”) + -ılda (verb forming suffix).
